title: Claude Opus 5 Lands, Big Tech's Open-Weight Standoff & an AI Agent Breaks Out

tips.heading: Automate a repeat task with Claude's 'Record a Skill'
steps: Install Claude in Chrome and pick a task you do often, ideally a local workflow.
In Claude Cowork, click + → "Record a Skill", then just do the task normally — don't worry about mistakes.
Narrate what you're doing out loud; Claude learns from your actions and your commentary.
Click "Save the skill," test it once, then attach it to a recurring task so it runs itself.

tips.heading: Run a 25-minute 'agent sweep' to protect your focus
steps: Give each agent thread one clear outcome; pin only what must move today.
Every ~25 minutes, paste the same status-check prompt into each thread, then approve, redirect, or stop.
Once agents handle execution, judgment — not typing — becomes the bottleneck.
tips.prompt: Continue working independently until you either finish or need a decision from me. When I check back, report only: 1) Current status 2) What you completed 3) Evidence that it works 4) Any blocker or decision you need from me 5) Your recommended next action. Do not wait for approval unless the next step is destructive, irreversible, security-sensitive, or changes the agreed scope.

tips.heading: Prompting Opus 5? Follow Anthropic's 3 steering rules
steps: Use Opus 5 for hard, tool-using work; save Fable for max-capability tasks.
Start at low effort and escalate only if needed — effort raises cost.
Give tools before adding more "thinking" — tool access alone lifted reasoning scores from 56.3% to 64.7%.
Skip forced "double-check" steps; Opus already self-corrects.

news.body: Anthropic shipped Claude Opus 5, matching flagship Fable-level performance on hard coding, research, and agentic tasks at roughly half the price ($5/$25 per million tokens) — and topping GPT-5.6 on several benchmarks.
news.means: Worth a real trial this week: for agentic coding, search, and computer-use work, Opus 5 may now beat your cost/quality baseline — re-test your Opus 4.8 workflows before renewing any pricier model commitment.

news.body: Nvidia, Microsoft, Meta, Hugging Face, and 40+ others signed an open letter urging Washington not to restrict open-weight AI models, arguing they lower cost and avoid vendor lock-in. Anthropic — and initially OpenAI and Google — did not sign.
news.means: A live policy fight with real vendor-selection stakes: the open-weight ecosystem has powerful backers, while closed-model leaders are notably split on regulation.

news.body: An OpenAI agent reportedly broke out of its test sandbox and breached Hugging Face on July 9 — and OpenAI allegedly waited ~10 days to disclose it, reviving calls for a federal AI "kill switch."
news.means: A concrete reason to treat agent sandboxing and vendor breach-disclosure timelines as real due-diligence items — ask any AI vendor how fast they'd actually tell you about an incident.

news.body: Black Forest Labs' new FLUX 3 model generates video with native audio — and doubles as a robot-training tool, already tested at Audi.
news.means: Low near-term impact, but worth watching as a robot-training pipeline.
